type.description: The message name — <name> in the routing key.

domain.description: The owning domain — <domain> in the routing key. Scoped to session rooms, and room-singular, so the key stops here: there is no <target> segment on any room-computers message.

kind.description: Which exchange carries this message. Never reaches the routing key.

ts.description: The PUBLISH instant — when this message went out, ISO-8601 UTC. There is no separate equality stamp: the document is the state, so two publishes compare by content.

propertyNames.description: A virtual name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (^[a-z0-9-]+$), no length limit.

machineName.description: The box's routing label — IRoutingConfiguration.MachineName, the label the backbone reaches the box by. Any non-empty string, NEVER PARSED: it is an OS observation (Windows shows hostnames upper-case). A reader compares it ordinal, ignoring case, and nothing else.

additionalProperties.title: Computer
additionalProperties.description: One computer in the room: the box a virtual name points at.

computers.description: Virtual name → the computer doing that job. Required and NEVER EMPTY: the Manager always publishes its own entry, primary-controller, though the wire does not require that key.

propertyNames.description: A group name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (^[a-z0-9-]+$), no length limit.

items.description: A member — a virtual name, a key in computers: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (^[a-z0-9-]+$), no length limit.

additionalProperties.description: The group's members. Each is a key in computers and appears once; the order is kept as authored and means nothing — a console may show it, never act on it.

groups.description: Group name → the virtual names in it. Required; may be an empty map, and a group may be empty. Group names and virtual names are separate namespaces.

RoomComputersStateChanged.description: The room's computers, by virtual name and group — the whole document, published at boot and on every change. computers is never empty; every group member is a key in computers and appears once per group. Names match ^[a-z0-9-]+$; machineName is never parsed.
